chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Ghiyāth ibn Kallūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, from his father عليه السلام, that ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say:
Regarding a chicken and the like that dies in the well, two or three buckets are drawn from it. But if it is a sheep and what resembles it, then nine or ten.

The proper way regarding this report is that we interpret it as indicating permissibility, and the first report as indicating merit and recommendation. Acting upon the first is preferable, because whenever we act upon the first report, this report is included within it, and our practice is then based on precaution and we attain certainty of taharah (ritual purity). But if we act upon this one, we would not be certain of taharah (ritual purity). It is also possible that the first refers to when it has decomposed, and the second to when it died and was removed immediately.

key_terms.الدَّجَاجَةِ: a chicken; the smaller animal discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الطَّهَارَةِ: taharah (ritual purity); the state sought through the ruling
key_terms.الِاحْتِيَاطِ: precaution; acting in the safer juristic manner
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation; a non-obligatory but preferred ruling
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is affected by the dead animal
key_terms.الْجَوَازِ: permissibility; the interpretive basis applied to this report
key_terms.الْفَضْلِ: merit; indicating the more virtuous course of action
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: is drawn out; refers to removing water from the well

ai.seo_question: How many buckets should be drawn from a well if a chicken or sheep dies in it according to al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This report discusses the number of buckets to be drawn from a well when an animal dies in it, distinguishing between a chicken and a sheep or similar animals. The compiler then reconciles the report with an earlier one by treating this narration as indicating permissibility, while preferring the earlier report as more precautionary and more conducive to certainty of taharah (ritual purity).
